LoloBuy ShipCare guide: coverage, exclusions and evidence

ShipCare can add route-specific protection to an eligible parcel, but it is not an all-risk guarantee. Check the event, item, declared value and evidence requirements before you pay.

Editorial note: This independent guide is based on LoloBuy’s public ShipCare and parcel after-sales materials, checked on 12 October 2026. Coverage, supported routes, rates and compensation promises can change. The live parcel screen and the terms shown for that shipping line control the purchase.

What ShipCare is—and what it is not

LoloBuy describes ShipCare as an optional paid protection service for parcels in international transit. The current introduction says the service was upgraded in August 2026 and can present four types of coverage: whole-parcel loss, damage or partial loss, customs seizure, and delivery delay. Availability is tied to the shipping line, so seeing one type on one parcel does not prove that every route or destination offers it.

The service is not a promise that any missing, damaged, delayed or seized parcel will be paid automatically. A valid claim must match a purchased coverage, happen during its coverage period, satisfy the route’s compensation promise and include the required evidence. Exclusions can apply because of the product, recipient action, customs compliance, address data, delivery status or the cause of damage.

Use ShipCare as a contract decision. Before purchasing, ask three questions: What exact event is covered? What maximum amount does this line promise? What evidence would I need if that event happened? If the live screen does not answer one of them, pause and ask support before dispatch.

Understand the four coverage types

Loss coverage

Loss coverage concerns a parcel lost during transit. LoloBuy’s current claim instructions require the parcel tracking number, proof of ownership and value, and a loss certificate issued by the carrier. For shopping-agent goods, the platform says it may verify the transaction internally; forwarded goods still need external proof. Tracking that shows delivered or successfully signed is excluded from a loss claim under the published terms.

Damage and partial-loss coverage

This coverage addresses damage to the parcel or missing contents during transit, within the purchased terms. The most important preparation happens before opening: LoloBuy requires a complete, continuous and unedited unboxing video that begins while the parcel is still closed and clearly shows the issue. Photos alone do not replace that mandatory video in the current rules.

The supporting file may also need the tracking number, proof of value, a detailed list of affected items and photographs of the package and goods. The official ShipCare page excludes electronic and 3C products from damage or partial-loss compensation. A buyer shipping those products should not assume that purchasing another coverage type silently creates damage protection.

Customs-seizure coverage

Customs-seizure coverage is narrower than “anything customs does.” The published exclusions say seizure caused by the recipient’s failure to complete local clearance procedures or pay required duties and taxes is not covered. Prohibited, restricted, hazardous or otherwise non-insurable items are also outside the service. Accurate item information and cooperation with customs remain the buyer’s responsibility.

Delivery-delay coverage

Delay coverage can be available on supported lines and may be claimed in addition to another covered event where the specific terms allow it. Do not invent a deadline from a past parcel or a different route. Save the delay definition and compensation promise displayed for the selected line before payment, because the current ShipCare introduction states that compensation can vary by shipping route.

How the current fee is calculated

At the time of this review, LoloBuy publishes a ShipCare rate range of 5% to 6%. The stated calculation base is the merchandise value plus the international shipping fee. A parcel with a combined stated base of RMB 500 at a displayed 6% rate would therefore show a RMB 30 service fee. This is an explanation of the published formula, not a quote for a future parcel.

Confirm the live rate, calculation base and coverage limit on the parcel screen. A fee calculated from merchandise and shipping does not mean every component is reimbursed in every event. The current terms say shipping-fee compensation uses the amount actually paid and excludes voucher or coupon value. Coverage is attached to the corresponding parcel and cannot be transferred to another shipment.

Declared value can limit the outcome

The declared value is not just a customs field. LoloBuy’s delivery agreement says the entered value is also used as a compensation basis if a loss occurs. The ShipCare rules add that compensation for a forwarding order cannot exceed the value the user declared. Under-declaring can therefore create a mismatch between the amount you paid for the goods and the amount available as a claim basis, while an inaccurate declaration can create customs problems.

Keep the declaration consistent with the underlying evidence: order record, invoice, receipt or transaction screenshot. Do not change the number merely to chase a tax assumption or a higher claim. Customs authorities apply destination rules, and ShipCare excludes losses linked to false information, prohibited goods or failure to follow clearance requirements.

Check whether the goods are insurable

The current non-insurable list includes intellectual-property-infringing goods; documents and certificates; tickets and travel services; securities, jewelry, jade, artwork, gold and other valuables; virtual or digital goods; tobacco products; vaccines, pharmaceuticals and controlled substances; plants, animals, frozen or fresh food; hazardous chemicals; flammable, explosive, corrosive or radioactive materials; and several categories of heavy, medical, semiconductor and precision equipment.

This is not a substitute for the full live list or the shipping line’s restrictions. A product can be accepted into the warehouse yet remain ineligible for a route or for ShipCare. Check eligibility after the final parcel contents are known. The shipping route comparison explains why product eligibility should be checked before price or delivery estimates.

Cancellation and coverage period

If the parcel is cancelled before it leaves the warehouse, LoloBuy says the purchased ShipCare coverage is cancelled and its fee refunded. Once the parcel has been dispatched, coverage takes effect and cannot normally be cancelled on its own. Domestic or international returns do not qualify for a ShipCare fee refund under the published policy.

The stated coverage period continues until the goods reach the destination named in the service order. Receipt or signature by the consignee or the consignee’s agent ends the coverage. Theft or loss after delivery is excluded. This makes the delivery record, correct recipient details and prompt inspection important parts of risk control, not administrative afterthoughts.

Build the evidence file before delivery

Do not wait for a problem before deciding what evidence exists. Save the parcel number, final declared value, purchased coverage, route-specific promise, item order records, payment proof, QC photos and dispatch details in one folder. For forwarded orders, retain the seller invoice or transaction screenshot because LoloBuy may not have the original purchase record.

When delivery is approaching, prepare to record the unopened parcel. Film the label, all sides and seals in one continuous shot, then open it without pausing and show every affected item clearly. Preserve the outer packaging, inner packing and labels until the case is resolved. If the box is visibly damaged at delivery, follow the carrier’s available damage-record or refusal procedure rather than relying only on a later explanation.

LoloBuy’s current ShipCare page gives a damage or partial-loss filing limit of three days after receipt. A whole-parcel loss claim must be filed within 30 days from the date of the carrier’s loss certificate. Use the live “Parcel Details – Protection Service” claim entry and do not delay while trying to perfect the evidence. For tracking-stage decisions, use the tracking status guide.

A practical purchase checklist

Confirm the line: verify that the selected route supports the coverage you want and save the line-specific compensation promise.

Confirm the goods: check every parcel item against the non-insurable and route-restriction lists, including electronics exclusions for damage claims.

Confirm the value: make the declaration consistent with purchase evidence and understand any compensation ceiling.

Confirm the event: distinguish loss, partial loss, damage, customs seizure and delay. Buying several coverages does not allow duplicate claims for the same event.

Confirm the evidence: know where you will obtain a carrier loss certificate and prepare to film an uninterrupted unboxing video.

Confirm the deadline: save the current filing window and submit through the parcel’s protection-service entry as soon as the evidence supports a claim.

Conclusion: buy terms you can prove

The useful question is not simply whether LoloBuy ShipCare is “worth it.” Compare the fee with a specific covered event, the route’s compensation ceiling and the evidence you can realistically produce. A clearly eligible parcel with saved purchase records and a planned unboxing video is easier to assess than a high-value parcel built on assumptions.

ShipCare may reduce part of a defined transit risk; it does not replace accurate declarations, compliant goods, correct recipient information or careful evidence. Read the live terms before dispatch and keep the records until the coverage period has ended. To research products before parcel planning, open FindSpreadsheet →
